decisions.why: The fallback loop (lines 167-196) re-requests imageinfo for titles the first loop already tried and got no URL for. Repair: keep a set of titles from the first loop and skip them in the second. Return values and prints unchanged; each skipped request is one Wikipedia round trip saved. Called only from get_car_image line 569.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: Batching titles into one imageinfo request needs the response pages mapped back to titles, which MediaWiki pageids and redirects make unverifiable offline. The first title succeeds on the common path, so batching would also add fetches there.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: requests.get opens and closes a new session per call, so each Wikipedia request pays a new TCP and TLS setup. Repair: one requests.Session inside the function, used for every search and imageinfo call in the same invocation (lines 86 and 88 alone would save nothing). Same headers, params, timeouts and exceptions.

decisions.label: d
decisions.why: Same readers as get_car_image label a: caching None blocks the similar-make fallback (lines 200-205) and makes a transient timeout permanent.

what_it_does: Turns preferences and facet filters into a Vespa ranking query, prints it, posts it with mTLS and returns the JSON results with car_id added, or None on error.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The print of json.dumps(query, indent=2) is printed output, which the contract forbids changing.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: A shared module-level Session would be used by threaded Flask handlers (app.run threaded=True), and requests does not document Session as thread-safe. A per-call Session saves nothing for one POST.

what_it_does: Builds a grouped facet query, prints it, posts it with mTLS and returns the JSON or None.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The print is printed output, which the contract forbids changing.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: Same as query_vespa label b: a shared Session is unsafe under threaded Flask handlers, and a per-call Session saves nothing.

what_it_does: Posts a nearest-neighbour query for one query text, retrying once on any exception, and appends the ranked hits to the global responses list.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The second post is a deliberate retry after the Retry adapter (total=20) gives up. Removing or narrowing the bare except changes which failures are retried and whether the run completes.

what_it_does: Posts a nearest-neighbour query for one query text, retrying once on any exception, and appends a positives and negatives record to train_data.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Same as evaluate.py search label a: the second post is a deliberate retry after the adapter gives up.

what_it_does: Creates a new storage.Client on each call and returns the lazy blob iterator for a bucket, used by listbucket, listfiles and getlogs.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: storage.Client() on every request repeats default credential discovery and builds a new authorized HTTP session. Repair: a lazily created, cached module-level client used by get_blobs; a failed build is not cached, and the return value is still the same lazy iterator. Called only at main.py lines 29, 43 and 58, each within its request.

what_it_does: Posts a fixed bm25 grouped query to local Vespa for one banking77 text and returns the parsed examples.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each requests.post opens and closes a new TCP connection to localhost:8080, once per row over up to 1000 rows. Repair: a module-level requests.Session used at line 211. Same request, response handling and printed output; the only caller at line 247 is single-threaded.

what_it_does: Exports an embedding model to ONNX, saves the tokenizer, then deletes every saved tokenizer file except tokenizer.json, printing each deletion.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The deletion loop prints one line per removed file, and avoiding the writes would change printed output and the set of files written. The saving is negligible next to the export.

what_it_does: Exports an embedding model to ONNX, saves the tokenizer, then deletes every saved tokenizer file except vocab.txt, printing each deletion.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Same as export_hf_model_from_hf label a: the printed deletion lines and the set of files written are part of the contract.

what_it_does: Groups order_products by order, merges the aggregated product lists onto the filtered orders for each eval set and writes orders_<eval_set>.jsonl with at most limit documents in sample mode.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Removing the second orders.csv read needs a frame shared through main(), a signature change beyond this unit. Moving the read into main would fail before the Processing users print on a missing file, changing printed output on that path.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: In sample mode the groupby with a Python list lambda runs over all eval-set rows (about 1.4M for train) when only limit orders are written. Repair: in sample mode keep df_order_filtered.head(limit) and filter df_order_products to those order_ids before the sort and groupby. The left merge keeps left order and the right side is unique by order_id, so the first limit rows are identical. Printed totals unchanged. Called only from main at line 412.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: iterrows builds one pandas Series per row; itertuples with attribute access gives the same int, float and notna conversions and the same text, so the written file is identical. Gains mostly in full mode, since sample mode stops after limit rows.

what_it_does: Reads products, aisles and departments CSVs, left-merges names onto products and writes products.jsonl with at most limit documents in sample mode.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Reading only the first limit rows before the merge is identical only if aisles.aisle_id and departments.department_id are unique, which the script does not enforce and the dataset CSVs are not in the repo to check. Saving is small.

what_it_does: Reads orders and the train order_products CSV, merges user_id onto each purchase, groups by user and writes users.jsonl with a per-user profile, at most limit users in sample mode.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Same as process_orders label a: sharing the orders.csv read needs a parameter through main(), and moving the read earlier changes printed output on a missing file.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: Restricting the merge to the first limit users needs the same full merge, and exactness depends on orders.order_id being unique, which the script does not enforce and the CSV is not in the repo to check.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: iterrows builds one Series per purchase row in every group. itertuples with attribute access gives the same int values, so purchase_struct and users.jsonl are identical; row order is preserved.

decisions.label: d
decisions.why: value_counts tie order sets the key order that json.dumps writes, so a groupby-based recount can change users.jsonl bytes.

what_it_does: Reads the docs JSON, converts each document's HTML to sections with html5lib and split_text, builds paragraph documents with question expansions and writes paragraph_index.json.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Switching from html5lib to lxml or html.parser changes the tree split_tables relies on: html.parser inserts no tbody, so table.find('tbody') returns None and line 118 raises AttributeError. Output changes on malformed markup.

what_it_does: Splits the markdown of a soup into (id, header, text) sections at each heading, appending each non-heading line to the current section's text.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: text = text + newline + line copies the whole accumulated section on every line. Repair: collect lines in a list and join once at each heading and at the final flush; the joined text is byte-identical and the empty case matches. Called only from main at line 157.

what_it_does: Returns the first tr inside the thead of the table containing a row, or None when the table has no thead.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Hoisting the header lookup needs state across calls, outside this unit. The in-unit alternative, find('thead', recursive=False), changes output when a nested table has a thead.

what_it_does: Escapes the text of each Jekyll xml highlight block by applying text.replace of the escaped block across the whole document.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The whole-document replace also escapes occurrences outside the block and re-escapes text the escaped form contains, so a per-block re.sub changes the output.

what_it_does: Reads indexed docids, optionally deletes all of them, computes the feed docid set, deletes indexed docs missing from the feed and feeds each file through the vespa CLI, printing progress.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: With do_index_removal_before_feed, line 177 DELETEs ids already DELETEd on line 158 with no PUT in between. Repair: guard line 177 with if not do_remove_index and keep the prints. The remote state is unchanged, and vespa_delete raises on connection failure before the second loop. Shipped configs set the flag to false, so the saving only applies when removal is enabled.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: Line 154 prints the count of docids_in_index unconditionally, so skipping the visit changes stdout.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: The shipped configs list several feed_endpoints sharing vespaapps_index.json, so get_feed_docids re-reads and re-parses the same files per endpoint. Repair: an optional feed_cache dict passed from main and used on a miss only. A failed read stores nothing, so the exception path is unchanged. update_endpoint has one caller, main line 201.

decisions.label: d
decisions.why: docids_in_feed = docids_in_feed.union(...) copies the accumulated set per index file. Repair: docids_in_feed.update(...); the set is local and used only for len and difference. An unknown doc type raises TypeError either way, with the same message.

decisions.label: e
decisions.why: The per-document To Remove print is stdout the workflow logs, so changing or merging it changes printed output.

what_it_does: Issues one HTTP DELETE per document id through vespa_delete and discards every response.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The parse is in vespa_delete (session.delete(url).json()), outside this unit. Dropping .json() stops a non-JSON error body from raising JSONDecodeError, which changes the exception type. Batching needs a different transport.

what_it_does: Sends one document to the Vespa document API by spawning a curl subprocess and returns curl's stdout bytes.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Replacing curl with requests changes the error path: call() ignores curl's exit code and lets curl's stderr through, so a connection failure is silent today, while requests would raise. Not identical outcomes.

what_it_does: Reads a feed JSON file, POSTs each document with vespa_post and prints each response body.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Batching changes the per-document printed output (line 86), which the contract forbids, and the transport change has the same error-path problem as vespa_post.

what_it_does: Prints a Removing line and issues one curl DELETE subprocess per document id.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Replacing the curl DELETE with requests changes the error path (curl exit code is ignored today), so outcomes are not identical.

what_it_does: Reads indexed docids via a visit, optionally deletes them, deletes indexed docs missing from the feed, then feeds each index file through vespa_feed while printing progress.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Skipping the second vespa_remove changes printed output (vespa_remove prints Removing per id) and, because vespa_delete ignores curl's exit code, a transiently failed first DELETE is only retried by the second one. Remote state can change.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The second parse is in vespa_feed (for doc in get_docs), not in this function. Removing it needs changes to vespa_feed and get_feed_docids, which are other units.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: docids_in_feed = docids_in_feed.union(...) copies the accumulated set per index file. Repair: docids_in_feed.update(...); the set is fresh and local, used only for len and difference, and get_feed_docids always returns a set here.

what_it_does: Loads processed query ids, then for each unprocessed query requests features and top hits from Vespa, appends annotated rows to the training CSV and appends each query id to the processed-queries file.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The processed-queries append runs for every query, including already-processed ones, so each rerun adds duplicate lines. Repair: move the with-open-append block under the if on line 75. The printed denominator is unchanged for a given starting file; only duplicate lines stop being written. The file is read only by load_processed_queries in this module.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: Membership on a list is O(P) per query. Repair: build a set after line 72 and test against it, keeping the list so len on line 72 is unchanged; int conversion errors are raised at the same point.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: The rows are written before the same query is recorded as processed. Batching the writes would let a crash record queries as processed with no rows on disk, so the on-disk state after an exception changes.

what_it_does: POSTs a search body to the Vespa search URL and returns the root children of the JSON response, or an empty dict after printing a message on a non-200 status.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: requests.post builds a new Session per call, so each of the two POSTs per query opens its own connection. Repair: a module-level requests.Session and session.post at line 38. Same return value and printed message; only the response cookies persist across calls, which nothing reads.

what_it_does: Reads each document's line from docs.tsv at the offset given in test-docs-offset.tsv, keeps lines whose id and field count match, and writes JSON lines to documents.jsonl in offset-file order.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Sorting offsets would make reads sequential but reorders documents.jsonl, changing its content; keeping order needs holding all documents in memory.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: json.dump uses the Python-level iterencode and calls write once per fragment; out.write(json.dumps(doc)) uses the C encoder and one write per document. Same text with default arguments, and all values are strings so no exception can occur partway.

what_it_does: Writes every document in the lookup table to docs.tsv via getcontent and writes each docid with its byte offset to docs-offset.tsv.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Writing fewer documents changes both output files, and sample-queries-and-documents.py select_documents samples from every key of docs-offset.tsv, so its output would change too.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: out.tell() on a text-mode file flushes the buffer and seeks once per document, about 3.2M times on the full corpus. Repair: track a running byte count from len(s.encode('utf8')) per document; the file is written in utf-8 with mode w, so the offsets are identical on Linux (newline translation aside).

what_it_does: Reads the doctrain queries file and returns query id to normalised text; the qrel argument is passed in but unused.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Skipping ids not in qrel saves work only if some queries lack judgements, which is not shown in the repo; the queries and qrels come from the same split.

what_it_does: Reads the queries TSV, normalises each query with a regex substitution and lower-casing, and returns a dict of query text and relevant doc ids.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Not output-identical: re.sub followed by lower() can produce a combining mark that the word class does not match, so the second pass changes some queries (for example U+0130).

what_it_does: Fetches the remote predefined_queries.txt on each call and returns its non-empty lines for st.selectbox when the checkbox is on.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: st.cache already used on line 23 would return the first fetched list for the life of the process, so later changes to the remote file would not be seen. The repo gives no evidence the file is static.

what_it_does: For each CLIP model in turn, builds a VideoFeedDataset and DataLoader over the videos and sends each batch of per-frame documents to Vespa, printing progress.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Decoding once per video needs a video-outer loop, which changes the order of printed progress and of the Vespa batches, or keeping all decoded frames in memory across models. The notebook calling this function would see changed output too.

what_it_does: Decodes a video's frames, converts each to PIL, encodes each frame with the CLIP image encoder one at a time and returns the per-frame Vespa documents.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Batching the frames would cut per-call overhead, but a batched forward is not guaranteed bit-identical to batch size 1 in float32, and the returned values are sent to Vespa, so the low-order digits could change.

what_it_does: Decodes every frame of a video at 1 fps into a list and returns the sample_images selection of number_frames equally spaced frames.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: For number_frames 0 the current path returns an array of shape (0, H, W, 3) with dtype uint8, while an index-first version returns float64 of shape (0,). The return value changes on that input. Decoding, the costly part, still runs over every frame.

what_it_does: Posts a batch of document updates to Vespa, prints the response summary and raises ValueError if any update failed, retried up to three times by tenacity.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: A targeted retry of failed documents changes the printed Successfully sent count and failure list, which the contract forbids.

what_it_does: Reads the user embeddings TSV into numpy float32 vectors and writes a Vespa feed JSON array with one put per user, each embedding formatted to six decimals.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Iterating a numpy array makes one numpy scalar per element; joining over embedding.tolist() gives the same float values in one conversion. '%f' of a float32 converts to the same Python float, so the bytes are identical.

what_it_does: Reads the news embeddings TSV and writes a Vespa update JSON array with one assign per news id, each embedding formatted to six decimals.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Same as convert_user_embeddings label a: join over embedding.tolist(), identical bytes.

what_it_does: For each unique docid, tokenizes title and abstract, runs one BertModel forward at batch size 1 and writes the first-token 512-float vector as a line, printing progress.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each forward builds an autograd graph and keeps saved activations. Repair: import torch and wrap the model call in torch.no_grad(); forward values are identical, and no graph nodes are allocated per document.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: outputs[0].tolist()[0][0] converts the full 1 x seq_len x 512 output to Python floats to keep 512 of them. outputs[0][0][0].tolist() yields the same 512 floats, so write_embedding receives an equal list.

what_it_does: Writes a tab followed by the embedding values, each formatted with %.4f and comma-joined, to an open file handle.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The loop issues about 1000 f.write calls per document. Repair: one f.write of the tab plus the comma-joined '%.4f' strings. The bytes are identical, including the empty case, and the only caller is create_embeddings line 59.

what_it_does: Streams a JSON array to news_category_ctr_update.json with one Vespa update per news id, each assigning the global CTR reference and a one-cell category_tensor.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The category_tensor string depends only on category, so a dict from category to formatted string, filled on a miss, gives the same bytes with one format per category instead of per item. Impact is low next to the file writes.

what_it_does: For one impression, fetches the user's embedding from Vespa, queries candidate news with it and returns the candidate predictions and the labels.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: A module-level dict from user_id to the user vector, filled on a miss, skips a Vespa round trip for repeated user ids. A failed lookup is not cached, so the exception re-raises at the same impression. calc_impression has one caller, evaluate.py line 88.

what_it_does: Reads the full impressions file, draws sample_size impressions with random.sample, scores each via Vespa and returns auc, mrr and ndcg.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Sampling before parsing keeps the random draws, but the repair stops validating unsampled rows, so a malformed row that raises today no longer raises unless sampled.

what_it_does: Parses every row of an impressions TSV into a dict with user_id, news_ids and labels and returns the complete list.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: calc_metrics needs every row in the returned list (len, enumerate, random.sample), so skipping parsing inside this function changes the return value; the only skip-parsing variant is the calc_metrics repair, which fails the exception check.

what_it_does: Returns the first Vespa hit child whose news_id equals the given id, or None.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The cost is candidate count squared per impression, small next to the HTTP calls. A dict index needs building in predictions, outside this unit, and it changes exceptions for children without news_id.

what_it_does: Computes normalised DCG at cutoff k for one impression by dividing the DCG of prediction-ordered labels by the ideal DCG.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The ideal DCG is computed once per call. The repeat is across calls (k=5 and k=10 sort the same labels), and sharing that needs state outside this unit.

what_it_does: Computes reciprocal-rank MRR for one impression from the prediction-ordered labels.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: One argsort per call. The repeated sort is across dcg_score and mrr_score callers, needing cross-call state; a negated-score argsort would change tie order.

what_it_does: Computes sklearn roc_auc_score per impression, averages them and rounds to four decimals.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The roc_auc_score call is the metric itself. A hand-written AUC changes float results in the last bits, and roc_auc_score raises for single-class impressions, which a replacement must reproduce.

what_it_does: Reads one impressions TSV, parses each row's time, user, history and candidates, and appends a dict with user_index, timestamp, news_indices and labels.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The timestamp key is unread in the repo, but strptime raises ValueError on a malformed date, and removing it lets the same input load without error.

what_it_does: Subsamples train impressions with prob, expands them via add_impressions and wraps the rows in a TensorDataset and a RandomSampler DataLoader for one epoch.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Each call draws new random subsample and negative decisions, so the epoch data differs per call. Caching would skip those draws and change the global random state later code sees. The per-sample lookups are in add_impressions, not here.

what_it_does: For one train impression, pairs each clicked candidate with sampled skipped candidates and appends user, news, category, subcategory, entity and label values to shared lists.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Lines 189-191 and 198-200 subscript self.news_content[idx] three times per generated row. Repair: bind content = self.news_content[idx] once per loop body and take the three fields from it. Values, order and the KeyError on a missing index are unchanged; sole caller is sample_training_data.

what_it_does: Builds a list of per-impression tensor tuples for the evaluation loop, optionally over the train set, keeping impressions with mixed labels and subsampling with prob.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: With train=True, the same tuples are rebuilt every epoch. Repair: a cache on self keyed by impression index, while still calling random.random() once per impression in the same order so the RNG stream is unchanged. Callers (train_mf.py:85, train_cold_start.py:124) only read the tuples. The cache keeps the train tensors alive for the process lifetime, a memory cost.

what_it_does: Parses each news row, collects WikidataIds from title and abstract entities, and stores category, subcategory and the first two entity indices per news id.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Dropping the second entity column is not pure: lookup_entity_index on that id registers it in entity_map, which changes num_entities (the nn.Embedding size) and later entity indices.

what_it_does: Runs the content-based model on each impression from sample_valid_data under no_grad, collects predictions and labels and prints group AUC, MRR, NDCG@5 and NDCG@10.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Batching or precomputing news embeddings changes the shapes of the Linear layers and the sum reduction, so the float outputs cannot be shown bit-identical, and the printed metrics are rounded to 4 places.

what_it_does: Computes the full user and news embedding tables from the model and writes them to data_dir as TSV files.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The recomputation and writes are the function's whole job; the waste is in the caller deciding to call it every epoch. No edit inside this body removes it. Handled by train_model label a.

what_it_does: Writes one line per id: the id, a tab, then the row values formatted with %.6f and comma-joined.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: embeddings[index].tolist() is a per-row tensor view and conversion. Repair: rows = embeddings.tolist() once before the loop and rows[index] inside. The float values and the %.6f join are unchanged, and a bad index still raises IndexError. The only caller is save_embeddings. Peak memory rises because all rows are converted up front.

what_it_does: Runs one epoch of minibatch training with BCE loss, accumulates batch loss tensors into total_loss and prints the total and average.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The printed line formats total_loss as a tensor, so the grad_fn repr is part of the output; changing its type changes printed text. The retained graph is negligible.

what_it_does: Runs the content-based training loop; after every epoch prints train and validation metrics via eval_model and rewrites the two embedding files through save_embeddings.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Only the embedding rewrite is guarded: if epoch == epochs - 1, so save_embeddings runs once after the last epoch. The evals stay, since they print and consume the global RNG. The final files are byte-identical and epochs=0 still writes nothing. Caveat: a run killed before its last epoch leaves no intermediate snapshot.

what_it_does: Runs the MF model on each impression under no_grad, collects predictions and labels and prints group AUC, MRR, NDCG@5 and NDCG@10.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Batching changes the shapes of the elementwise multiply and the sum, so last-bit float changes can flip a printed 4-place digit. Not verified by a run, and it holds all impressions in memory.

what_it_does: Seeds the RNGs, loads MIND data, trains the MF model, evaluates the final model on train and valid, prints both metric dicts and saves the embedding TSVs.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: When the last epoch already ran the 10-epoch evaluation, the two stored metric dicts can be printed instead of re-running eval_model on identical weights, saving one full train-set pass and one valid pass. Printed lines identical. train_model and eval_model have no other importer; no random draws follow these calls.

what_it_does: Runs the MF training loop with fresh negative samples each epoch and every tenth epoch prints train and validation metric dicts.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The train-set dict is printed, and sample_valid_data draws random.random() per impression, which advances the global stream used by the next epoch's training data. Removing or moving the call changes the trained weights.

what_it_does: Posts a nearest-neighbour news search with the user vector, candidate filter and timeout to Vespa and returns the parsed JSON.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: requests.post opens a new connection per call; repair: a module-level requests.Session used for the post, keeping the same data body, timeout field and exception types. Callers are evaluate.py line 53 and user_search.py line 18, which read only the JSON. The module-level session must be created by this repair itself, not borrowed from another unit's repair.

what_it_does: Queries the Vespa user source for one user_id over HTTP with the optional mTLS cert and returns the first hit's embedding values.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: requests.get opens a new connection (and mTLS handshake) per call; repair: a module-level requests.Session used for the get with the same cert argument. Return value and exception types unchanged. Callers are calc_impression and user_search.py line 17.

what_it_does: Builds the Vespa query body for the first-phase feature collection, with nearest-neighbour clauses, query text, ranking and two embed inputs for the int8 and float query tensors.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The embed() strings are evaluated server-side. The two keys feed differently typed tensors (tensor<int8>(x[96]) and tensor<float>(x[768]), base-features.profile lines 3-4), and the profile reads both. No Python edit fills both from one call. Step 1 listed lines 49-50 for this unit; the embed keys are at 95-96, and 49-50 belong to feature_collection_second_phase_query_fn.

what_it_does: Builds the Vespa query body for the second-phase feature collection, with the same clauses and two embed inputs.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Same check as the first-phase function: server-side embed strings for two differently typed tensors, both read by the profile. Step 1 listed lines 95-96 for this unit; the embed keys are at 49-50.

what_it_does: Builds the Vespa query body for learned-linear ranking, with nearest-neighbour YQL, query text, hit count, linear weights and two embed inputs.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Server-side embed strings for two differently typed tensors, both read by the inherited profile. No Python edit can fill both keys from one embedding; production hybrid.xml sets both to embed(@query) too.

what_it_does: Builds the Vespa query body for second-phase GBDT ranking, with nearest-neighbour YQL, query text and two embed inputs.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Same as rank_first_phase_query_fn label a: two server-side embed inputs for differently typed tensors, both read by the profile.

what_it_does: Builds the match-only query body over nearest-neighbour clauses with the query text and one embed input for the int8 tensor, called once per query by each evaluator in a module-level loop.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The embedding is computed server-side per request, so Python has no vector to share. Caching responses across evaluators is not identical: the hybrid YQL adds userQuery, so results differ, and skipping calls changes the timings the evaluator records.

what_it_does: Builds the match-only query body with nearest-neighbour clauses plus userQuery, called once per query by the hybrid evaluator.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Same as match_semantic_query_fn label a: the embed is server-side and cached responses differ from the semantic and weakand responses.

what_it_does: Stratified k-fold LightGBM training on the CSV features with categorical encoding and feature renaming, logs CV metrics, then trains and writes a final model with original feature names restored.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Removing lgb_train from valid_sets removes the train metric from the log_evaluation output printed every 100 rounds, which changes printed output; early stopping inputs also change.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: One Dataset with subset per fold keeps the parent's bin boundaries, while the per-fold Dataset bins on the fold's training rows. Histograms, trees and metrics change, so it is not identical.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: Sequential re.sub over the whole string can rename a name that a later entry also matches, and it rewrites dictionary keys such as feature_infos. A single dict walk does not give identical output on every input.

what_it_does: Loads the CSV, prints per-feature statistics, runs 5-fold stratified logistic regression, prints summary tables and saves the coefficient expression.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Direct mean, std, min and max calls give the same numbers for numeric columns, but describe() has no mean key for object or bool columns, so the exception type and printed output change on those inputs.

what_it_does: For each batch of ImageNet images, saves missing JPEGs, computes DINOv2 CLS embeddings from the re-decoded files and feeds the records with feed_iterable, logging progress.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The embedding would be computed from the pre-save in-memory image instead of the quality-88 re-decoded JPEG, so the vectors change. The refeed path has no in-memory image at all.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: Moving the exists check above ex['image'] changes the exception path for a bad existing file and moves some skips into total_skip, changing the logged progress records.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: One feed_iterable call changes the cadence of the per-batch progress records and the failure-reporting order. The pyvespa setup cost was not verified.

what_it_does: Tokenizes the query and writes a Vespa query body as JSON to stdout, with token ids and attention mask as float lists.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: np.array(..., dtype=float32).tolist() gives the same floats as float(i) per element for integers below 2^24, and json.dump writes identical text. Repair: drop numpy from this function and build the float lists directly. Not confirmed here that the vocabulary stays below 2^24; numpy stays in requirements because model2onnx.py uses it.

what_it_does: Builds a graph that concatenates the query with each of two documents, passes each pair through a shared linear and sigmoid, and returns a score; reached only through torch.onnx.export.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Splitting the linear into query and document parts reassociates the float sums, so outputs are not bit-identical and the exported pairwise_ranker.onnx changes. The Java side loads that artifact.

what_it_does: For one query group, takes the query text from the group (last row wins), posts one hybrid search request and appends one record per hit to the global responses list.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Replace the loop with query = query_group['query'].iloc[-1]; the loop leaves the last row's value, so the value and type match. Removes one pandas Series per group inside a Python loop. Groups are never empty; search has one caller, line 75, which discards its None return.

what_it_does: Parses arguments, opens a requests Session with retries, reads the query TSV, runs search over each query group in order and writes the hits to a .run file.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Parallel groupby.apply would reorder the appends to the global list unless results are re-collected in order, and requests.Session is not documented thread-safe. The gain is wall-clock only; energy benefit is not established.

what_it_does: Reads product lines from stdin, converts each to a Vespa put with process, skips failing lines and prints the list as indented JSON to stdout (the README writes it to feed_items.json).

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Streaming stdin changes stderr progress records on malformed UTF-8 (readlines fails before writing progress). Dropping indent=2 changes the bytes written to feed_items.json. Both fail the same-output contract.

what_it_does: Reads review lines from stdin, converts each to a Vespa put (None for illegal characters), counts skipped lines and prints the list as indented JSON.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Same as convert_meta main: streaming changes stderr progress on malformed input, and dropping indent=2 changes feed_reviews.json bytes.

what_it_does: The flush method of the file-like Log object that pexpect calls after each write of a read chunk, flushing sys.stdout so output appears as it arrives.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: pexpect calls flush on every chunk, so the method must stay. An empty body changes when stdout bytes are emitted and how they interleave with stderr ERROR lines, which is observable output timing.

what_it_does: Applies each regex in liquid_transforms in insertion order via re.sub to one command block and returns the rewritten text.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The per-key substitutions are sequential by design, so merging them into one alternation can change results. re.sub already caches compiled patterns, so precompiling saves almost nothing.

what_it_does: Parses the HTML page into a script dict, prints a header and the whole script as indented JSON, then executes it.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The printed script is printed output, which is part of the contract, and the print is not gated by verbose, so removing or gating it changes stdout in the default run.

what_it_does: Prints a header, fetches each comma-separated entry (urlopen for http, file read otherwise), concatenates the bytes in order and passes them to process_page.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Keep-alive via http.client changes exception types that run_config depends on (HTTPError vs RuntimeError). De-duplication changes the concatenated bytes within one comma list, and a cross-call cache would return stale content. The configured entries are local paths, so the urlopen path is not exercised anyway.

what_it_does: Downloads one PDF with up to max_attempts tries, derives a safe filename, writes it under pdfs/ and returns the path or None.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: When the safe filename is '_', continue runs before attempt += 1 and the loop re-GETs the same URL forever with no sleep. Repair: increment attempt before continue so the branch counts toward max_attempts and the function returns None. That branch never wrote or returned before, so every terminating input is unchanged. The original does not terminate on this input, so the harness may report it as blocked.

what_it_does: Converts a dict of float embedding rows into a dict of int8 lists holding the sign bits packed eight per byte, one list per key.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: About four numpy calls per row per page become a few whole-array calls: stack the rows, compare with 0, packbits along axis 1, astype int8, then row.tolist() per key. Keep the original loop as fallback for empty or ragged input. packbits on axis 1 equals per-row packbits, and the last-byte padding matches. Only caller is line 611.

what_it_does: Runs the ColPali model over the page images through a DataLoader and returns one numpy array of per-page patch embeddings, with batch_size meant to group images.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The DataLoader is built without batch_size, so the batch_size=2 parameter is ignored and the model runs once per page. Repair: pass batch_size=batch_size. The collate function uses padding to a fixed length, so batch composition does not change sequence length. Batched matmuls may change float rounding in the last bits, and the iteration count changes.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The premise is wrong: np.concatenate converts each view with one bulk copy, so the same bytes are copied either way. Removing the per-image view saves microseconds against a full model forward.

what_it_does: Sends one page image and the query prompt to Gemini and returns the parsed JSON dict of queries, or six empty strings on any error.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Reusing saved queries needs a reader of output/pdf_pages.json, which has none (the reader is commented out). Reusing stale output replaces fresh LLM output, and the empty fallback would be cached as valid. Concurrency changes the function to async and breaks its caller.

what_it_does: Encodes a PIL image to JPEG at default quality and returns the base64 text.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The input is already decoded here, so the stored bytes are not available. Returning base64 of the original bytes changes the return value for every caller. Avoiding the decode needs a change at the module-level load_dataset cast and in process_item_for_vespa.

what_it_does: Maps one dataset row to a Vespa document dict with base64 JPEG images and an embedding dict rebuilt from embedding.N columns.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Raw stored bytes (decode=False, set at module-level line 15, outside this unit) give base64 of different bytes than today's re-encoded JPEG, so the returned blur_image and full_image change for every page.

what_it_does: Resizes a similarity map, colours it with viridis and returns it as a base64 PNG string; the img argument is never used.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Dropping the unused img parameter removes a reference, not work, so there is no energy mechanism. The base64 round trip is a separate change that alters the yielded type across colpali.py and main.py, not folded into this repair.

what_it_does: Builds a zero float32 tensor of shape (maps, query tokens, patches, patches) and fills it with each Vespa summary cell at its token and patch position, skipping patches past the sequence length.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The loop does one torch element assignment per Vespa cell, each with dispatch overhead. Repair: collect values in a dict keyed by (idx, token, row, col) with last-wins semantics, hoist the image_seq_length lookup, then write them with one index_put_. The output tensor, dtype and values are unchanged; out-of-range rows still raise IndexError. Only caller is colpali.py line 91.

what_it_does: Runs the ColPali model on the query and returns its embeddings and a map from position to token string taken by decoding the ids and re-tokenising; cached per query string.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: convert_ids_to_tokens gives identical strings only if decode then tokenize returns the same sequence, which the code does not establish. Spacing cleanup or sentencepiece normalisation could change the token count, changing the mapping for some queries.

what_it_does: Returns True when a query token matches a fixed set of filter patterns (special tokens, whitespace, punctuation, leading underscore, the word Question, a lone sentencepiece space).

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: re.compile on a constant is served from re's internal cache, so the removable work is the per-call cache lookup. Repair: a precompiled pattern, returning the same bool for both callers. Saving is small (about 100 calls per query), so it is likely to measure as negligible.

what_it_does: Loads each input image as RGB with a copy and its size, computes normalised similarity maps per query token and yields each non-filtered token's blended PNG as base64.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Only the size is needed downstream, but _load_image wraps decode failures as ValueError through convert('RGB'). A lazy size read would accept corrupt bodies that raise today, changing the exception contract.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: processed_images is never read. Removing it saves no work, only residency of decoded pages, so there is no energy mechanism.

what_it_does: Converts each query-embedding vector in a dict into a sign-bit packed int8 list, keeps at most 64 entries and logs a warning at 64 or more.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The unit accepts any dict of lists: an empty dict returns {} today, and ragged rows convert one by one, while a stacked array raises. A one-shot numpy version needs fallbacks for those inputs. The work is at most 64 rows, so the saving is small.

what_it_does: Converts a query-embedding tensor into a dict mapping each row index to that row as a Python float list.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The per-row work is the enumerate comprehension calling tolist per row. Repair: for a torch.Tensor input, return dict(enumerate(q_embs.tolist())), keeping the old loop for other inputs. Same keys and values; a 0-d tensor still raises TypeError. Readers are query_vespa_bm25 and query_vespa_colpali, both in this file.

what_it_does: Fetches the base64 full_image field for one document id from Vespa and returns it as a string.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: pyvespa creates and closes an httpr.AsyncClient on each context entry. Reuse needs a long-lived client with an owner that closes it, which cannot be built inside this unit without private pyvespa methods.

what_it_does: Runs the _sim ranking query through asyncio.run and returns the summaryfeatures value of each hit.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The duplicate query comes from main.py, where fetch_results and get_and_store_sim_maps each query Vespa with the same q_embs. Removing it needs the first response passed from main.py, a caller change beyond this unit.

what_it_does: Runs a regex match over the questions field for a query string and returns the unique questions found.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Same pyvespa lifecycle as the other session items: a new AsyncClient per call that only a long-lived owner can reuse, outside this unit.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: questions is attribute-only with no index (pdf_page.sd lines 50-52), so the substring match changes the result set if replaced by a prefix or contains form; a prefix index needs a schema change.

what_it_does: Sends the query text, an optional qt tensor and the bm25 or bm25_sim ranking to Vespa and returns the JSON response.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: pyvespa creates a new AsyncClient per context entry (VespaAsync __aenter__/__aexit__), and a shared client needs an owner outside this unit; this method also runs on a separate event loop via asyncio.run in the sim-map path.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The bm25 profile in pdf_page.sd reads query(qt) only inside the function used by bm25_sim. Repair: include input.query(qt) only when sim_map is true. Non-sim BM25 calls stop converting and serialising the token-by-128 tensor. Sim queries still send it. Not verified against a running Vespa.

what_it_does: Adds a None-valued sim_map placeholder field to every hit for each non-filtered token and returns the children list.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Deciding whether a sim-map file exists needs query_id and SIM_MAP_DIR from main.py, which this method does not receive. The None value is the signal the frontend uses to choose the polling button.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: should_filter_token runs in a list comprehension once per call over idx_to_token, not per hit, so the claimed per-hit cost does not occur.

what_it_does: Builds the About This Demo component, including the Hugging Face dataset viewer iframe.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The returned component tree is rendered directly by main.py; adding loading=lazy changes the returned markup, which the contract covers.

what_it_does: Builds the disabled spinner button for a pending sim map that re-requests /get_sim_map on a fixed interval.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Changing hx_trigger changes the returned markup and how long a finished map waits to appear, which the contract covers.

what_it_does: Builds the Vespa logo as two img elements (light and dark), inside a sized Div.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Any single-image repair changes the returned markup. A picture element with a media query would show the wrong logo, since the theme is set by localStorage and a dark class, not the OS preference.

what_it_does: Returns an HTML img with the full JPEG of a document as a data URI, fetching from Vespa and writing to disk on a miss, or base64-encoding the disk copy on a hit.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: On a disk hit every request reopens the JPEG and base64-encodes it. Repair: an lru_cache-backed helper keyed by path returning the same base64 string; the miss branch is unchanged. Route called only from app.py line 638; the readers of the files do not use this cache. maxsize bounds memory.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: Batching is set by the frontend issuing one request per result (app.py line 638), outside this unit. Coalescing concurrent misses would skip the debug log line for the waiting request and change the number of Vespa queries.

what_it_does: Hashes the query and ranking string into an integer shown as query_id in sim-map ids, file names and log lines.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The value is visible in returned ids, URLs and file names, so a stable hash changes every returned value. No work stops, since nothing reads a cache keyed by query_id before generating.

what_it_does: In a background thread, runs a second Vespa query for summary features, waits up to 5 seconds for the full images and writes one blended PNG per document and non-filtered token into SIM_MAP_DIR.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Every non-filtered token gets a button that polls for its PNG, so the PNGs are needed for this search's UI. Deferring them moves work to the poll path and changes which files exist at search time, outside this unit.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The second query is a duplicate with an identical ranking, but removing it needs changes to get_fields, get_result_from_query and fetch_results in main.py, which is beyond this unit. A candidate for a cross-unit change.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: An early return on existing outputs skips the Vespa query and the saved debug records, and cannot see index state; the query_id hash is salted per process, so reuse only helps within one process.

decisions.label: d
decisions.why: The 0.2 s sleep is off-CPU and bounded to about 25 wakeups per search. Changing the interval changes when maps appear, which the contract forbids.

what_it_does: Starts a background task at startup that calls a Vespa keepalive query every 5 seconds and logs each call at debug level.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The periodic query is deliberate: the vespa_app keepalive docstring says it keeps the connection alive, and main logs each tick. Changing the interval or stopping it changes the queries issued and the debug records.

what_it_does: Streams Gemini's answer over server-sent events, after waiting up to 10 seconds for the full images, converting newlines to br tags in the accumulated text.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Image.open is lazy and reads only headers, and the wait loop stops once enough images exist, so the reopen work is a few header reads per tick. Keeping handles open across ticks changes what is read when the file is still being written.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The replace reruns over the whole accumulated text on every chunk, which is quadratic in the reply length. Repair: replace in chunk.text only and append the converted piece. A single-newline pattern gives the same string, and the replacement contains no newline, so no new matches.

what_it_does: Imports the Space app with a test client, checks three routes return 200 and, with --load-model, asserts the LoRA-B weights are non-zero and the query embeddings are finite 2-D with width 128.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The LoRA-B checks build autograd graph nodes for each parameter, since loaded parameters require grad. Repair: wrap the check in torch.no_grad() or use detach. Assertion results and messages are unchanged; the model is local to main. The saving is small.

what_it_does: Base64-decodes a JPEG string, opens it with PIL and saves it, which re-encodes it as JPEG at default quality.

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Writing the decoded bytes directly changes every file in hf_dataset/images, since the current output is a second JPEG generation. The dataset is pushed to the Hub, so published bytes change too.
